customManagers.description: skalibs, pinned by commit with its tag as a comment. skarnet versions are A.B.C.D, which semver-coerced cannot order (it offered only same-tag digest updates), so the versioning says so: a change in B is skarnet's incompatible bump and arrives as a Renovate 'minor'.
s6, pinned the same way as skalibs.

xpra -- the display server the native Porthole viewer speaks to -- installed into the shared base image from xpra.org (it is not in Debian). This file is the ONE place the version lives: base/Dockerfile takes it as a build arg and pins the whole xpra package SET with it, and generate-viewer derives the launcher's compat major.minor from it. The deb datasource reads xpra.org's own trixie Packages index.

packageRules.description: skalibs and s6 move in ONE PR: each s6 release is built against its own skalibs (s6 2.15 is an 'adaptation to skalibs-2.15'), so either bump alone fails to build and neither could ever land. Not an automerge exception -- automerge is the family default (ship-if-green) and still applies; build/check-transport.sh is what makes green mean 'the shipped s6-ipcserver works', not merely 'it compiled'.

xpra is the family's ship-if-green exception, because a bad bump BUILDS FINE AND IS WRONG: the native viewer is written against a specific xpra wire protocol, and a newer xpra installs cleanly while silently changing it. No green build can catch that -- the launcher's check_xpra_compat only nudges the user to rebuild, it does not fail. So bump xpra deliberately, together with the viewer. Renovate still opens the PR, which is the point: before this, nothing was watching xpra at all and the pin rotted until a release-time build went red.
